rationale: Whole dried celery extract improved some beam and grid outcomes in MPTP mice. The Parkinson mixed diet reports a motor total. These measurements give no fresh celery leaf effect on stride length.
access_or_open: Primary mouse results and mixed-diet appendix checked. A confirmed fresh-leaf, measured stride comparison remains open.

rationale: A methanolic dill aerial-parts extract inhibited rat ileum contractions in vitro. A sowa withdrawal study measured locomotion and rotarod performance. Neither experiment assessed neurological dystonia after ordinary dried dill weed.
access_or_open: Exact human neurological dystonia evidence remains open for culinary dried leaf.

rationale: Oral sweet basil extracts reduced motor impairment in mouse ischemia models, including inclined beam performance. Related publications vary occlusion duration and treatment timing. The human mixed diet gives a motor total without basil-specific stride length.
access_or_open: 2009 poster checked. The 2011 and 2018 journal studies have author abstract and publisher preview access. Numeric motor estimates and cohort overlap remain open.

rationale: Oral extracts reduced immobility or improved selected stress behaviors in rodents. The feed study had inconclusive sucrose preference, and an earlier tincture report describes no forced-swim activity. These comparisons leave a clinical direction after dried culinary tarragon unresolved.
access_or_open: Original Persian report confirms powdered dried leaves used to make an extract. The 2019 animal study may share animals and has a different outcome.

rationale: A historical article reports attempted hallucinogenic use without a verified case, exposure or visual effect. Parkinson dried-leaf tea reports a nonmotor total. Acute rat observations after concentrated extract do not measure hallucinations.
access_or_open: Verify the source behind the historical mention and obtain the visual-hallucination component from the Parkinson pilot. The 2007 collection body remains pending.

rationale: The thyme-containing massage blend protocol registers facial anxiety in intensive care. Both groups in a Parkinson diet trial ate from thyme-containing menus and the trial reports a motor total without a facial-expression item or separate thyme effect.
access_or_open: Oil massage, rated anxiety expression and the clinical Parkinson masking endpoint remain distinct. The registry has no posted results.

rationale: Basil is listed in a mixed Parkinson diet with an improved motor total. Fresh preparation, actual intake and listener-rated speech intelligibility are unresolved. Rodent basil extract studies measure motor tasks without a speech outcome.
access_or_open: Original diet and UPDRS methods accessed. The 2026 animal paper provides separate extract and levodopa arms in the displayed tables.

rationale: Isolated anethole delayed a rotarod fall in toxin-exposed rats. The ground-anise trial reports general adverse symptoms without a fall count. A vitamin D protocol registers everyday falls, with aniseed ether among comparator excipients and no posted results.
access_or_open: Recorded animal and clinical outcomes are different, and the registered protocol does not isolate ground anise. The 1908 issue scan needs verification.
